provenance.prompt_summary: Generate the Level-1 child module refining the F3 AEB branch of the vehicle-level ADAS SOFL model from NL-RQ-ADAS-v1; single pass, no self-review.

elements.name: TTC_Computation
elements.responsibility: Compute, for each predicted object, the TTC to the ego vehicle and report the minimum TTC over the object set together with the number of objects considered.
invariants: The AEB capability is guaranteed for ego_state.speed <= 130.0 km/h (N-1).
elements.notes: The empty object set is reported with a count of 0 as required by section 6; no sentinel value for min_ttc in that case is specified by the spec and is therefore left unconstrained (see OI-16). Section 5 also gives F2 the TTC duty (see OI-7).

elements.name: Risk_Classification
elements.responsibility: Classify the situation into a risk level as a function of the minimum TTC and raise the driver warning for caution and critical.
invariants: warning.active = 1 whenever ttc_set.min_ttc <= 2.0 s (N-2 warning present no later than the 2.0 s staging point)
elements.notes: Risk codes: 0 = no risk, 1 = caution, 2 = critical. Warning codes: 0 = none, 1 = caution, 2 = imminent collision. The traffic rules are read from the parent store D4 (logical reference, no store element in the child CDFD).

elements.name: Maneuver_Planning
elements.responsibility: Produce the cruise/keep-lane, deceleration or emergency deceleration manoeuvre from the risk level, respecting the driver intent without overriding the emergency manoeuvre.
preconditions: risk_level <> null and ego_state <> null and driver_intent <> null and route <> null and HD_Map_DB <> null
invariants: For the critical risk level the required deceleration is at least 6.0 m/s^2 and the target speed is 0 (A-1).
elements.notes: Manoeuvre codes: 0 = cruise / keep-lane, 3 = lane-keeping-with-deceleration, 4 = emergency deceleration. The caution case with a driver acceleration request is ambiguous in the spec and the explicit caution rule is modelled (see OI-8).

traceability.note: Exactly three sub-functions refine the emergency-braking capability of F3.
TTC per predicted object, minimum TTC over the set and the number of objects considered; count 0 when no object is considered.
Risk classification by minimum TTC and the driver warning for caution and critical.
Cruise/keep-lane, deceleration and emergency deceleration manoeuvres; the emergency manoeuvre is not overridden by a driver acceleration request.
The AEB branch is guaranteed up to 130 km/h.
Warning raised at TTC <= 2.0 s and at latest at the 2.0 s staging point; T_fcw = 1.5 s.
The 6.0 m/s^2 emergency deceleration is sized from the N-3 impact-speed yardstick.
Sizing basis only; the 60-130 km/h VUT window and the 20 km/h target speed are assessment parameters without a runtime element (see OI-14).
The RSS safe distance has no closed form in the spec; the emergency deceleration covers the dangerous case, the formal distance bound remains open (see OI-9).
The braking profile is covered by A-1 >= a_min,brake = 4.0; the response time rho = 0.1 s is not formalised (see OI-13).
Emergency deceleration of at least 6.0 m/s^2 with target speed 0 for the critical risk level.
The branch consumes the 3.0 s prediction horizon produced by F2; A-7 is realised in the parent module.
Each sub-function has a precondition, a postcondition and a quantified constraint where a threshold exists.
Level-1 clauses are traced to the child elements.
The nat code tables and the parent-store logical references are declared as modelling conveniences.
Each flow is named, directed and has a single producer and a single consumer.
ttc_set is consumed by F3.2, risk_level by F3.3, warning by E7 and manoeuvre by the parent F5.
Every datum read in a postcondition is guarded by an explicit <> null precondition.

open_issues.issue: The seven-function split of section 5 is sufficient for the stated ODD only if driver monitoring stays an external input: no separate driver-monitoring function is added because R-L0-1 forbids extra elements, but a full SAE L2 handover would need one.

D3 ownership is accepted as specified (written by F1, read by F6/F7) because section 5.1 assigns those reads explicitly and R-L0-1 forbids a dedicated ego-state function, so F1's update rate becomes a safety dependency of the shield.

A timing requirement is needed for the emergency branch to be meaningful: the spec fixes thresholds but no cycle time, and SOFL has no timing construct, so rho = 0.1 s (A-2) and the derived 1.39 s braking duration are not formalised.

The AEB branch of F3 is a defensible Level-1 refinement, but refining the F6/F7 actuation chain would cover N-7 and R-E-2 better, because the numeric lateral-acceleration capability and the response time are both missing there.
Section 5 makes F2 the only TTC-computing function while section 6 has F3.1 compute a TTC set, so TTC is computed twice and the responsibility split between F2 and F3.1 is left unresolved.

Section 6 requires a non-zero deceleration manoeuvre for caution but also gives a driver acceleration request precedence for every non-critical risk level, so the caution case with an acceleration request has no consistent rule and the explicit caution rule is modelled.
N-5 does not restate the RSS minimum-safe-distance formula and fixes no unit convention, so the safe-distance requirement is modelled qualitatively instead of as a numeric distance bound.
N-7 has no numeric lateral-acceleration capability in section 7/8, so the branch cannot check the commanded lateral acceleration of a trajectory it does not receive.
The RSS response time rho = 0.1 s cannot be expressed because the SOFL expression grammar and the CDFD have no timing construct.
The N-4 assessment parameters (VUT 60-130 km/h, target 20 km/h) describe the test scenario rather than a runtime constraint, so they have no model element.
Enumerated values (risk level, warning type, manoeuvre type) are encoded as nat codes because the permitted expression grammar contains no string literals; the code tables are listed in README.md.
The spec fixes the object count 0 for an empty object set but no sentinel value for the minimum TTC in that case, so ttc_set.min_ttc is left unconstrained whenever the count is 0.
